references.text: The preceding verse describes that two cherubim of gold are to be made, which verse 19 continues to elaborate on regarding their placement at each end of the mercy seat.
The next verse continues the description of the cherubim and explains how their wings are to be spread upward to cover the mercy seat.
Bezalel carries out the instructions from chapter 25 and makes the two cherubim, one on each end of the mercy seat.
Solomon made two cherubim of olive wood for the innermost room of the temple, reflecting the cherubim on the ark of the covenant.
The cherubim in Solomon's temple spread their wings over the place where the ark of the covenant stood, showing continuity in cherubic iconography from the tabernacle.
Ezekiel's vision of the cherubim with God's glory connects to the presence of the cherubim at God's throne above the mercy seat.
The book of Hebrews refers to the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat, a direct reference to the cherubim described in Exodus 25.
A direct parallel between the instruction (Exod. 25:19) and the execution (Exod. 37:7) of the cherubim on the atonement cover.
